pr.title: Make MIR cleanup for functions with impossible predicates into a real MIR pass
pr.description:
It's a bit jarring to see the body of a function with an impossible-to-satisfy where clause suddenly go to a single `unreachable` terminator when looking at the MIR dump output in order, and I discovered it's because we manually replace the body outside of a MIR pass.

Let's make it into a fully flegded MIR pass so it's more clear what it's doing and when it's being applied.
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The PR is a pure refactor: it moves the existing impossible-predicate body erasure from inline code in `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked` into a registered `ImpossiblePredicates` MIR pass. The frozen analysis and the decoded MIR diffs confirm the body transformation itself is byte-for-byte unchanged (`bbs.raw.truncate(1)`, clear statements, set `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`, clear `var_debug_info`, truncate locals to `arg_count + 1`). The only change is pass ordering/naming in MIR dumps; the final optimized MIR for functions with impossible global predicates is semantically identical before and after the PR. There is no historically incorrect value transformation to encode—modeling `unreachable` erasure as "wrong" against a normal body would invent a bug the PR never claimed or introduced, since the pre-PR compiler also erased such bodies (just earlier, outside the pass pipeline). Consequently no source-grounded original/transformed function pair with differing concrete behavior exists. Manufacturing one (e.g., returning tuple values vs. diverging) would violate the requirement to encode only the actual wrong transformation.

analysis.summary: The PR moves pre-existing MIR body erasure for functions with impossible global where-clauses out of inline code in `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked` and into a registered `ImpossiblePredicates` MIR pass in `run_analysis_cleanup_passes`. The body transformation is unchanged; the improvement is that the cleanup is now ordered/visible as a real MIR pass in MIR dumps. This is a refactor/optimization, not a confirmed bug fix: the supplied patch adds a new mir-opt test showing before/after pass states rather than changing output from a prior correct state.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the PR, `mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked` contained the impossible-predicate check inline: it collected `tcx.predicates_of(body.source.def_id()).predicates`, kept only `p.is_global()` predicates, elaborated them, and if `traits::impossible_predicates(...)` returned true, it manually cleared the body. The original function body for the test is ordinary MIR that copies `_1` into `_2`, creates mut references `_3`/`_4`, and returns them via `_0`. The PR retains this exact predicate logic and body-erasure logic but extracts it into a `MirPass`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically the body replacement was performed manually outside the MIR pass pipeline, described by the PR as: "I discovered it's because we manually replace the body outside of a MIR pass." That placement made the body suddenly become a single `unreachable` when viewing ordered MIR dumps, without an explicit pass naming and positioning the change. The corrected transformation is the same body-erasure operation, but executed as `ImpossiblePredicates` in the pass list, with pass-level MIR dump naming. Do not invent a different predicate or body rewrite: the diff shows identical cleanup semantics, only the pass registration/placement changed.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions that can be written with impossible-to-satisfy where-clauses, notably under `trivial_bounds` such as `fn foo() where String: Copy {}`. The pass only considers global predicates; generic/non-global predicates such as `<T as Foo>` are filtered out. The supplied test uses `pub fn impossible_predicate(x: &mut i32) -> (&mut i32, &mut i32) where for<'a> &'a mut i32: Copy`.
analysis.trigger: The trigger is: after elaborating the function's global predicates, `traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, ...)` evaluates to true. Then the pass logs `found unsatisfiable predicates for {:?}` and erases the body. Normal functions without impossible global predicates do not trigger it.
preconditions: The MIR body must belong to an item whose `predicates_of(body.source.def_id())` contains global predicates after filtering with `p.is_global()`.
The filtered predicates, when elaborated, must be recognized by `traits::impossible_predicates`.
The pass runs during analysis cleanup, registered immediately before `CleanupPostBorrowck` in `run_analysis_cleanup_passes`.
pitfalls: Do not treat all where-clauses as candidates: the pass filters with `if p.is_global()`, because non-global/generic predicates cannot reliably be proven unsatisfiable in a generic context.
Filtering non-global predicates also avoids normalizing predicates involving generic parameters (e.g. `<T as Foo>::MyItem`), which the source says can confuse normalization and cause cycle errors.

The erasure must leave exactly one basic block: `bbs.raw.truncate(1)`, clear `bbs[START_BLOCK].statements`, set the terminator to `TerminatorKind::Unreachable`, clear `body.var_debug_info`, and truncate `body.local_decls.raw` to `body.arg_count + 1` so the return place and arguments remain.

Do not conflate this body erasure with borrowing logic: the test's `&mut` references merely make the input body non-trivial; the pass condition is the impossible where-clause, not borrow restrictions.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a mir-opt test with `// skip-filecheck` and `// EMIT_MIR impossible_predicates.impossible_predicate.ImpossiblePredicates.diff`, where the test function has an impossible global where-clause such as `for<'a> &'a mut i32: Copy`. The resulting `.diff` must show the before-pass body with locals, debug info, and normal statements, and the after-pass body reduced to one `bb0` containing `unreachable;`, no `debug` locals for `x`/`y`, no non-argument locals, empty `scope 1`, and only the return place retained. The diff naming ties the test to the concrete pass ID `ImpossiblePredicates`.
